productPageReviews.reviewTitle: Incredible, Solid, and Easily Transportable. A Product I Would Not Want To Live Without Now.
productPageReviews.reviewDescription: Incredible product. Much more solidly built than I had expected.I purchased this because my 2017 MacBook Pro I-7 would warm up considerably during heavy work (I am a data scientist and push the machine to crunch very large sets before I move a project over to AWS for its computing power). This product was more than I expected. It is light weight, strong, and folds conveniently into a size that fits in an outer pocket of my backpack, thus I carry it with me wherever I go. Even when I am not crunching numbers, I place my Mac on it. The typing angle is perfect for long coding sessions and makes my hands feel much better.The item does adjust for the size of the laptop. My MacBook Pro is a 15 inch, but my ASUS laptop is a 17 inch. With a quick turn of the pressure dial on two of the legs, the X-stand adjusts between my Mac and ASUS so that each has a SOLID platform to rest on. And the room below the machines is ample to provide good airflow to keep the machines cooler.I wholeheartedly and enthusiastically recommend the X-Stand, especially if your "office" is more often on your back and your workstation is any desk surface you can find like mine tends to be. It conveniently folds into a small size and provides an adjustable, solid platform to air your laptop. I may purchase additional ones so for when (as too often happens) this great product is discontinued - should it every be - or for holiday gifts for my other geek friends.
productPageReviews.reviewedIn: Reviewed in the United States on March 21, 2018

productPageReviews.reviewTitle: LIGHT WEIGHT, ADJUSTABLE, and PACK-ABLE stand!
productPageReviews.reviewDescription: I bought this stand because I was going to be mobile a lot with my laptop and needed something that wasn't going to bulky when I packed it , but would lift my pc when I would game to allow good ventilation.I am currently using this on a  and it works great! It lifts the pc without putting any marks or scratches on the computer and it does allow better viewing angles with it if your using a keyboard separately( which is two of the reasons I got it for.)The stand seems to made out of aluminum and is okay in relevance to the price. . if they would have made it 1/64 " or 2/64 " thicker it would have felt even sturdier, but I guess it would have cost more for them, and then for you.Being 23 dollars when I bought it I think they should at least increase the thickness by that much to better it but, as it is the product is good.It is easily adjustable to your laptop since it has numbers on the sliders which stand for inches of your laptop so you can easily slide and lock to your size and not have to eyeball it every time.One of the other things I wish they would have done is added rubber instead of the soft plastic they added on the ends.That way over time you could replace the heads if your moving a lot AND you would have way more grip than the stand currently offers.Apart from these two reasons which would make the product better, this stand is fantastic compared to the ones with the fans that are really thick, hard to pack, and dont really do much except add noise.

productPageReviews.reviewTitle: Best $30 I Ever Spent For My Laptop
productPageReviews.reviewDescription: Durable aluminum construction. Adjustable for multiple laptop sizes. No big bulky cheap plastic cooling pad to lug around, which effectively defeats the purpose of the portability of the device I need it for. This stand folds up into a very compact form factor that fits perfectly into one of the pockets in my laptop bag, no fuss, no problem. No useless fans that generally never improve temperatures in any meaningful way that the fans in the laptop don't already accomplish themselves if they have ample room to breathe, not to mention promoting more dust and dirt getting pushed into the laptop vents, all at the expense of more fan noise and using up one of the already scarce USB ports on the laptop to power them, therefore no mechanical moving parts that will inevitably break or die.This is getting use with a 17.3" MSI Stealth GS76 laptop sporting a Core i7 11800H and a 16 GB RTX 3080 - This laptop gets mighty hot during gaming sessions, and sometimes even during general tasks when sitting flat on a surface. I already have to max the fans to 100% during gaming sessions so as it is. I'm always trying to prop something under the rear outer edge of the laptop to elevate it a little for better airflow, what a pain. This little stand has solved all my problems and really helps a lot to allow the fans in the laptop to work more effectively, pulling much more airflow through the vents underneath, as well as more room for hot air to exhaust away from it, and has such a small footprint where it makes contact with the underside so as not to block airflow into the vents. I get incredibly better cooling results with this stand.My only complaint related to this stand is directed at myself because I didn't get one sooner. It's exactly what I've had in mind and have been looking for.
productPageReviews.reviewedIn: Reviewed in the United States on December 30, 2024

productPageReviews.reviewTitle: PERFECT Stand/Easel for iPad Pro Artists and Creatives!PERFECT Stand/Easel for iPad Pro Artists and Creatives!
productPageReviews.reviewDescription: So since the iPad Pro release I've been on a mission to find a good stand to simple prop the iPad up a bit for sketching.  I'm a product designer by trade so I'm not doing insanely intricate work (mostly concept sketching) and after years of sketching a Cintiq, I'm used to sketching at somewhat of an angle.  I originally purchased a stand that was marketed as an iPad Pro/Macbook Air Stand from a much more expensive (almost triple the cost) and well-known brand, but it fell short in more ways than one.  THIS, however, is perfect for iPad Pro sketching.  It works so well that in fact, I'm going to also write the seller to make sure they add it to the description.The problem with the "other" stand(s) is they simply aren't portable.  Why would you want to buy a huge clunky stand (yes it might be pretty and textured aluminum and Apple make it more appealing by offering it in their online store) and not be able to just throw it in your bag?  The Steklo X-Stand features very well thought out design and construction along with the portability you want for the products it supports.  I do have one small gripe however, and that is the "feet" at the bottom that stabilize the laptop (by your wrists if you were typing) are a bit long.  They stick out above the edge of the iPad Pro but for MacBook Pro customers this probably wouldn't be a huge deal depending on what model/how you type.  For me personally I will probably Dremel them down a hair shorter so they're flush with the screen (I'm on the fence though as they do offer a good place to rest the Pencil) and still do their job of holding the unit in place.  In all reality the feet haven't really bothered me yet on a physical level (I've only been using it for a few days) so I guess it's more of an OCD thing.  The feet and back supports are soft polymer that provide plenty of grip/stability and I don't see them scratching any type of metal, but I use a case regardless.If you're looking for a great way to prop up your iPad Pro for sketching/drawing/painting whatever, you've found it!  Don't go blowing all kinds of money on a more expensive stand when it's simply not necessary and lacks portability.  I've added some customer images for anyone who'd like to see it modeled with an iPad Pro.

productPageReviews.reviewTitle: Very good workhorse for business but poor display quality is an issue for streaming
productPageReviews.reviewDescription: It pains me to give this Lenovo only three stars, since for the most part, it has good specs for a fairly budget-conscious laptop. It has an excellent, quiet AMD Ryzen processor and generous, upgradeable storage capacity, all of which contribute to smooth performance and speed for multi-tasking with more than one application open at once. So why three stars instead of four? Because this laptop's one fault, the one thing that the builders skimped on, is so major that it almost cancels out its good qualities. I'm talking about the poor quality of the display. It's described as full HD or FHD, backlit LED with 1920 x 1080 resolution. Unfortunately, these nice-sounding specs don't make up for the weak Radeon integrated graphics card, which delivers mediocre to poor images with washed-out, untrue colors. It's as if you're looking at old faded photographs, and the anti-glare matte finish doesn't help. The integrated graphics do not allow for enough manual adjustability to improve display quality. So try as the user might, there's only so much the built-in graphics card can do.All that said: This is a great laptop for business. Text documents are crisp, especially if you use the Windows text clarity function, where you can adjust the sharpness of the text according to your own eyesight. Also excellent for business or home-office use are all the different ports and slots. It even has an ethernet port, which is handy to have if you need reliable internet service but live or work in an area where internet strength can be spotty.  This laptop is also surprisingly light and thin, so another plus is that it has excellent portability.Conclusion: This is a handy, budget-conscious laptop for business use from the reliable and well-established Lenovo brand. But don't choose this laptop if streaming movies and seeing bright, vivid, true colors are also a priority. If you want an all-around workhorse that can double as a streaming device, you'll need to spend more money and get a laptop with a dedicated graphics card.

productPageReviews.reviewDescription: I was a little suspicious given the lack of any reviews and the Q&A section response linking to a model with different specs. However, I was pleasantly surprised that the product description on Amazon is mostly accurate:17" 1080p IPS 144hz GSync matte displayIntel Core i7-9750HNvidia Geforce RTX 2070 - I believe this is the laptop variant of the 2070(higher clocks than Max-Q)16GB(2x8GB) DDR4 memory  - User upgradeable, 2 slots totalSamsung 256GB M.2 NVMe SSD - Doesn't seem to be user upgradeable though I didn't look too carefully.1TB 7200RPM SATA HDD - User upgradeable(mine was a seagate barracuda but this could vary)Intel wireless AC4 zone RGB keyboard - The zones are left 1/3, middle 1/3, right 1/3, WASD keys.Trackpad with physical left and right buttonsI/O Ports - Custom power plug, Ethernet, HDMI, Mini-DP, USB-C, 3 USB-A SS, SDCard slot, Headphone, MicrophoneOverall this is a great laptop for gaming. The everyday price is actually pretty good considering the specs you are getting, so would be a great deal if it ever goes on sale. The old saying "you get what you pay for" is really true here. Nonetheless, the SSD should be ~500GB instead of 256GB, and the sound quality should be better. Make sure you swap out the HDD with a large SATA SSD and you should be good to go.This is a full blown gaming laptop, which means it is big and bulky, the power supply is big and bulky, it will get hot and the fans will run loud, the battery life will be abysmal. These are a given for legitimate gaming laptops and hence I'm not going to hold any of that against it. To be fair I haven't even tried it on battery so can't really speak to the battery life.The gaming performance is pretty good. For e-sports/casual/old games getting a locked 144fps  at 1080p medium/high shouldn't be a problem. For newer/AAA games you will probably get 80-120fps at 1080p medium. Lowering graphical settings won't help much as you will probably be CPU/Platform limited at this point and due to the thermal/power constraints of a laptop there isn't really any way to solve this. With GSync this is still not bad, and it may make sense to up the graphic settings and go for a more consistent lower fps vs a higher fps with more variability.Complaints:Sound quality - For a laptop this size meant for gaming, the sound is disappointing. There is literally no bass whatsoever; I'm not expecting a full sub but at least some bass for something this size. Note that there is a software equalizer/DSP in the Omen audio control and if you find it hard to hear voices, you can adjust it.Primary drive too small - The SSD is 256GB, it really should have been in the 500GB range for this price.The viewing angles on the screen - It is an IPS display but the viewing angles seem more limited than on most IPS panels I've used. For a single user shouldn't be an issue though.Left "Ctrl" key on keyboard when gaming - It is a bit too far left because of the "Fn" key to the right of it. My pinky doesn't like stretching out that far in the WASD position. I can still game fine but would have preferred the keys swapped or some other solution that brought the Ctrl key to the right just a bit.No auto-adjusting screen brightness - Doesn't have an ambient light sensor to adjust the brightness automatically.Note: The one I purchased had an issue where the keyboard's left RGB zone's blue light was stuck on. The replacement doesn't have this issue and is working well so far.

productPageReviews.reviewDescription: We bought one of these and got a good deal!  Our old HP Elitebook is still doing fine for us, but of course cannot be upgraded to Windows 11.  Thus, we bought this "renewed - excellent" laptop for the Win 11.  There really weren't any printed instructions in the box, so we just had to look up some help online on setting up hp Windows 11 laptops.So far, setting it up and starting to use it, it seems to be a really nice unit.  It's fast and quiet - the 16GB of ram seems very adequate, and the 1TB solid state drive is fast and larger than we'll ever use.  We use the card reader socket to save all our user files on an SD card for easy portability between desktop and laptop.  It has 3 USB's (could have a couple more), video out, and audio I/O.  The wi-fi was easy to set up, the Radeon video does the job nicely, but it took a little figuring to get the monitor output working as an extension of the laptop screen.Other than getting used to Windows 11, the only thing we don't like is the keyboard and buttonless touchpad.  They don't work and feel as nice as on the old Elitebook.  Maybe we'll get used to them, or maybe we'll get a wireless external keyboard and mouse.All in all, a nice computer. Hopefully MS won't come up with a reason we can't upgrade the it to Windows 12 or 13 when needed!

productPageReviews.reviewTitle: many good things, but a few downsides
productPageReviews.reviewDescription: First, it was a good value.Second, it's light.Third, it's got a bunch of unique control buttons along the top, one of which turns the sound on and off and has light to show when the sound has been disabled, and two others which turns the volume level up and down.  These are Windows operation versions of the F1-F12 buttons.Fourth, it's got plenty of RAM and plenty of storage space for me.  Although the fact that OneDrive defaulted to ON caused some problems, because the OneDrive does come with nearly enough storage to back up even half of this laptop's memory.  So I had to disable OneDrive.  I have a physical backup drive which can accommodate all of this laptop's memory already.Fifth, at least for now, it's got great battery life, many hours of normal operation before it starts going into power saving mode.Sixth, it's nice that it has Bluetooth, because I was able to find a Bluetooth mouse, and that's a bit easier to use than a USB cable mouse.But the touch-pad with no separate buttons is a little hard to use, because it doesn't have an edge scrolling option like my previous laptop did.And there's no place to plug in an Ethernet cable, so I have to hope that I can get close to that network speed with WiFi.  The built-in WiFi works OK, but when I take the laptop to another room in my apartment from where my WiFi router is, I get slow response if I don't orient the laptop in just the right direction.And while it only has a solid-state disk, not a physical hard disk, the fan noise is just about as loud as the fan plus the hard disk was on my previous laptop back before my previous laptop developed fan problems.And while my previous laptop was Windows 10 and never asked to me to restart until it was REALLY ready to install something, this Windows 11 laptop keep telling me I to restart, and if I restart immediately I have to restart again, and again, again, all for the same update.  So it seems to be asking too early to restart.  So I have experiment with how much I need to delay the restart to see when it will only need to do the restart once.And finally, it's hard to know which exact user guide is right for this.  This is a 2023 laptop, but I was only able to find 2022 and 2025 User Guides for this type of HP laptop.

productPageReviews.reviewTitle: Great Buy, was what i expected it to beGreat Buy, was what i expected it to be
productPageReviews.reviewDescription: Keep in mind that this is more of a rant, and I'm half asleep, but this is what I've gone through so far with the product.Originally came from an hp g62 2010 - 2018, was able to make the laptop last. Finally wanted to upgrade and saw this on sale, so I went for it and it was what I wanted in a laptop for what I do: Music, School, Youtube, Slaughtering Demons.The rant and rave of an individual:The screen is very nice, I can confirm it is an In-plane Switching Monitor or (IPS) as I do not have to center the screen or move my body to get a great view of it, unlike a lot of TN panels that I've used back in the day. The disassembly of the device is very very simple, remove the screws from the bottom of the case and the case pops off, might need a thin tool to pry the case off a bit (only con here) and you'll see the ram and the hard drive and the nvme along with the fans which make it easy for upgrades and cleaning. Also the battery is not soldered into the board and easily comes out for replacement after you remove some screws. All screws I noticed were Phillip's head. (I like to watch disassembly videos in case something happened, that way I can tear into it and hopefully fix the issue.) The ram is decent for 12 gigs, a 4 gig stick and an 8 gig stick, but I plan on upgrading the ram soon. Now after uninstalling a few things and setting windows to use less resources, I idle at about 18-19% which isn't bad at all, depends on what you do though. I do believe the manufacturer specifications have tested up to 16 gigs of 2666 on the board, however; there are cases with other omen laptops, where you can plop in 16 gigs in each dimm slot for a total of 32 gigs, wouldn't recommend it because it's not officially supported, but I will go ahead and try it (making sure i'm at the latest bios update from hp), and will provide an additional review/update. (I like to run a lot of things at once.) The processor is very nice, windows shows that i have 4 physical cpus and 8 logical processors, and I idle at 0% after turning the thing on (which mine booted into windows less than 3 seconds with the nvme 128 gig harddrive).  I plan on upgrading the nvme from 128 gigs to 1 terabyte, might clone the drive or just grab a fresh install of windows 10 and slap it on a usb drive and fresh install, go from there. From what I read on the specification sheet for the dc0010nr, I think a cap of 512 Gigs nvme was officially tested and supported, but I'm going another 512 and see how the machine fairs. The 1 terabyte hard drive isn't slow at all, but I have nothing on it but a few games and some music, I constantly keep it defragged.  The sound on the laptop is definitely an upgrade from my old hp g62 via software and hardware, but i use headphones into the 3.5mm jacks for mic and playback anyways.  when it comes to gaming: Doom 2016 gives about 100 to 130fps on 1080p, ultra + open glide settings.... battlefield 1 on 1080p ultra gives about 45+ on mp and 60+ sp, drop it to high and it gives about 60+ but it depends on what map and what all is going on via gameplay. The heat on the laptop isn't bad, the machine will get warm and the fans will kick into high gear almost like a delay, but there is absolutely no throttling and when i'm finished with my gaming, the fans kick off to silent almost immediately. Also with the gpu, this is a verified gtx 1050 ti with 4096MB of vram in it.Final note:I think it's worth what I payed for: 799.99. If my desktop crashes and burns, it's a great replacement for it. It absolutely destroys solitaire and minesweeper along with other office products like excel spread-sheeting and you're in need for a couple of Pareto diagrams or 3 point beta distributions to resolve employee padding with P.M.O affairs making sure the stakeholders are happy. Alas I digress... I unboxed it, i pressed the power button and it immediately shot into windows and was ready to go. :)

productPageReviews.reviewTitle: Great little mobile laptop.  Buy the renewed ones for great value
productPageReviews.reviewDescription: It's small and cute.  Nice ice blue color (rather than plain silver).  Display isn't bad even if it isn't full 1080P.  Battery life >> guess it's ok since you can't fit big batteries in this small footprint.  Computing power is adequate for business use (MS Office) but not photoshop stuff.  I will use my ipads for that.So I haven't used windows PC for about 6, 7 years since I quit my company office job and didn't need Microsoft Office or any business apps.  Was using ipads for most of my web activities, which is pretty good.However, I have once again started some jobs that require office apps and decided on this "renewed" Surface Laptop Go (I first purchased Surface Go 3, but it didn't quite stand up to my needs for office use).First of all, "renewed" isn't like what you see on ebay or craigslist.  It's professionally packaged, just like Apple refurbished products that you purchase directly from Apple.  Mine had almost 10months warranty remaining.  Battery capacity was 100%.  It's just great value to go for renewed.  The price also has dropped considerably now.  I think you can get if for less than $500.It's a great value.  Again, if you just need basic computing needs, don't do any graphics intense stuff like video editing or games (although it does some games quite well), and don't mind the small screen, and need to take your laptop with you at all times, this is perfect.By the way, when I work at home, I do have an external display.  I purchased a 24" monitor for about $150.  With dual monitor set-up, it really boosts your productivity.  All this for less than $800.  Super happy that I purchased this.So, just crossing my fingers that there won't be any issues with it in the long run.
productPageReviews.reviewedIn: Reviewed in the United States on April 30, 2022

productPageReviews.reviewDescription: OK, I'll admit: I was extremely skeptical when buying this "renewed" laptop. I can't tell you how many times I've bought a "refurbished" device only to receive something that looked and performed like it had been to war. Echoing what others have said, this is the exact opposite. My laptop came well-packaged and it comes in Microsoft Certified Refurbished white box. It was even packaged like it was brand new with the plastic wrap on the device and accessories (which were also new). Furthermore, there were no signs of wear or use on the laptop. It looks like a brand new device. I checked the battery health (both with Windows and Linux) and both report the battery at 100% health. In fact, Windows had the cycle count at 2.For the laptop itself, I'm very impressed with the Surface Laptop Go. I was coming from a Chuwi laptop, which was good in its own right, but I can't believe how premium this laptop is. It's fast, well-built and handles anything I need to do on it. Admittedly, I was worried about the display resolution, but after using the device, I can say it was unfounded. The display on this thing is fantastic. Where it falls short on the resolution numbers, it makes up by being a fantastic panel. The keyboard and trackpad are great. I understand that people miss the backlit keyboard, but that's a non-issue for me. I usually turn that feature off to save on battery. The sound quality is also great. It's loud with good clarity. I can't speak on the battery life, yet, but it seems average so far. Being a Microsoft device, Windows 11 is a pleasant experience. However, if you're a Linux fan (like me), you'll be happy to know that everything works out of the box.Overall, I am extremely pleased. The condition, value and performance of the laptop are all fantastic. I can't speak of the longevity of the laptop, but everything seems great so far. Sure, there are better value options out there (Chuwi, Alldocube, etc.) in this price segment, but I worried about the quality control with those devices. I would definitely purchase this again.

productPageReviews.reviewDescription: I have already a Chromebook but needed a budget Windows laptop for basic web-surfing, email, Youtube, and some Word document creation. I read many of the reviews saying how slow this machine is but I thought, how bad can it be? It might be slow for gaming, video streaming, or downloading large files -  but I'm not planning on doing any of that thus this little laptop should be fine for me.  WRONG! This machine is excruciatingly slow! If you enjoy watching for minutes a piwheel every time you click on a website link, by all means, go ahead and get one - or better yet, get two and gift the other to someone you really dislike. It took me about 9 minutes to watch a 1.5 minute Youtube video. This laptop will test your patience and will to live.  After testing it for several very frustrating hours, I packed it up and the very same day send it back. However, please be aware that you will be charged "Restocking Fee Refund Deduction: ($52.00)."  This should a real embarrassment Lenovo or anyone else trying to sell this in 2020.

productPageReviews.reviewDescription: Very happy with this purchase, as my old laptop was..old. The only purpose for my purchasing this laptop was to pay bills online and to communicate with family and read the occasional e-mail.Light weight, simple interface, small enough for most backpacks, sling bags, etc.I didnt purchase this for gaming or for media consumption, simply a simple terminal for simple needs and the price point was spot on!Its is fairly thin and extremely light, almost to the point I feel I need to pamper it, but probably don't.The OS is Windows 10, which is all I need and with minimal tweaks got everything to a satisfactory setting (loving dark mode).Is it worth your money? Depends on your use for it. If you just need a simple terminal for your day to day activities, that's what I think it's great for, if you're looking to play MMOs or download your entire discography, maybe a PC is what you're looking for.

productPageReviews.reviewTitle: Good EXCEPT for one horrific design flaw
productPageReviews.reviewDescription: Lately I’m so dependent on my laptop I get anxious at the thought of being deprived of it for even a day or two.  I needed an inexpensive backup machine with basic functionality (MS Office, middling speed internet access) in case my higher-end Lenovo is unavailable.  Here’s how this one compares with my custom T470:--Unbelievably Boneheaded placement of the power key. It's on the keyboard jammed in with the backspace and delete keys, as if they want you to hit it accidentally as often as possible.  This is textbook-worthy design incompetence.  No way I could live with this as my primary laptop.  Really unfortunate, because otherwise this looks like a great machine for the money.--display: clear and bright, non-glare, large enough to avoid eye strain; however, extremely sensitive to viewing angle--for most Office tasks the lower speed is noticeable but not too bad--wireless connectivity: I struggled to connect with Bluetooth and wifi-enabled devices, but it finally worked--as expected, it can’t handle 100 MB OneNote files; they have to be broken down into smaller ones-- battery life minimal

productPageReviews.reviewTitle: Not really refurbished. Used is more accurate.
productPageReviews.reviewDescription: First of all, and importantly speaking, the laptop works, more on that later. It is about all the good I can say. Though it would also protect other Amazon customers, I am not at liberty to say which 3rd party vendor I purchased this laptop from here on Amazon.  The laptop is supposed to be refurbished, not necessarily used. Most reputable refurbishers will actually refurbish a laptop with new or like new parts. It's not enough to just spray windex on a machine and wipe it off and blow compressed air into a laptop and voila, it is refurbished. This laptop was apparently in very rough shape, so someone painted it. When I took the laptop out of the box, it had a very strong paint odor and you can see places with overspray all over the laptop. Also, someone put a piece of vinyl on the top to hide some of the scratches and damage. It was definitely NOT excellent or close to excellent condition. The screen was dirty, the touchpad shiny and in the center of the touchpad, it doesn't register touch properly. The laptop also apparently had some liquid spilled into it on one side as a couple of the keys would make a crackling sound and sometimes stick. When you have a dark background on the screen, you can see hot spots and visual defects in dark mode. Light mode kind of hides it, to an extent. The SSD is heavily worn with a remaining life of 73% and the battery had a remaining life condition of 77%. The industry norm is over 80% for both. The charger was also some off brand charger that works most of the time, until it gets hot and no longer charges the laptop. We had a project where we needed a laptop and couldn't really afford to be down any longer than we were, so we opted to keep this rather than go through the hassle of return and be down longer. Paid $360 for the laptop and then later had to order a new touchpad, keyboard, bottom panel, SSD, battery and charger for an additional $300. Also had to clean out all of the dust and reapply new thermal paste to the processor to keep it cool and not overheat. We really honestly should have just bought new. At least now, with all the extra expense, it basically now qualifies as a truly refurbished laptop.

productPageReviews.reviewTitle: Priced like a Chromebook, but is instead a fully functional PC.
productPageReviews.reviewDescription: If you are looking for an inexpensive laptop, this one definitely works as such. It's priced like Chromebook, but it is just a normal, inexpensive PC.Some of the laptop's specs are expectedly minimal, having tiny storage space and minimal memory. It does sport a full 1920x1080 screen but the screen is not particularly bright or clear. I find the screen useable, particularly when using "dark mode" settings, but it's clearly not a highlight of the machine's hardware.It has a reasonable keyboard. It has two USB A slots, one USB C slot, one HDMI port, and a traditional audio port; its battery charge seems to be good for about 9 hours of light use.The wireless works reasonably well. The speakers are lackluster in sound quality, but are sufficiently loud to hear clearly. Music sent out via the audio port is surprisingly good quality. The processor is a good compromise, offering a reasonable amount of value for a very small price. I find the overall weight for the laptop good. The laptop doesn't dissipate heat as well some laptops, but it's not unpleasant to hold.If you are using Linux, all of the hardware works well with a modern distro. You wouldn't want to compile a full, traditional Gentoo system on this machine, but any of the modern mainstream binary distros should be fine.

productPageReviews.reviewTitle: Great computer. EXTREMELY EASY to remove S ModeGreat computer. EXTREMELY EASY to remove S Mode
productPageReviews.reviewDescription: I feel the need to counter the most popular review here because it is misleading to new customers, and could potentially prevent them from buying a great little computer. If all you want to do is browse the internet and stream Netflix, etc, this is the perfect computer. Please note that you likely won't be able to play many games or use video editing/other resource-intensive software on this thing, that's not what this is for.To remove "S Mode" (aka safety mode), all you need to do is go to your Start Menu, type "s mode", and follow the instructions. It's so easy to set up. You only need to do this once! See images.All S Mode does is prevent the user from downloading any program that isn't on the Microsoft store. Most people don't want that, and the computer doesn't function as expected with it on - to someone familiar with computers, it doesn't behave like a computer!*However*, I wish this setting was around while my grandfather was alive. He didn't understand that downloading random slot machine games from unvetted sites could expose him to viruses. If he were locked into only downloading from the Microsoft store, it would have saved 2 computers he destroyed.So: if you're familiar with computers and are looking for something blazing fast that's lightweight and can handle Microsoft Office programs, browsers, and video streaming without issue, this is the one for you. Screen is great, battery life is great, and charging through a USB-C port is incredibly convenient (assuming your phone charger is a decent wattage, you can charge your computer with that, too!). I got it here for less than $300 and it was a steal.And, as I said, if you have someone in your life who would like to use a computer but isn't familiar with the dangers of downloading programs from shady websites, S Mode could be of genuine value to you. My grandfather even fell victim to a computer lock-out scam towards the end of his life that cost him hundreds to resolve. Something to consider.

productPageReviews.reviewDescription: I haven't owned this long but so far, I like it.  If you're tech savvy, you can make this into a great little laptop for a steal of a price on Prime Day.  By itself, it's a little underpowered. The RAM is supposedly not be upgradable because the RAM is hardwired to the motherboard.  8 GB of ram is totally fine for this anyway.  This isn’t a creator computer by any means.  The 128GB M.2 ssd drive is replaceable. I have a 1TB M.2 drive to replace it with.  It comes with Windows Home in S mode, but anytime you want you can flip a software switch in windows and it becomes regular Windows 11 home.  This is not reversable however, so make sure you really don’t want the S mode version.  (You can do your own research on S mode)  Now you have a fine laptop, fully decked out for home computing and browsing use.  You can’t beat it for $279 plus a little extra if you want a larger ssd stick.

productPageReviews.reviewTitle: Nice laptop but the Tylvx installed software is a huge problemNice laptop but the Tylvx installed software is a huge problem
productPageReviews.reviewDescription: This Tylvx Professional Laptop appears to be a rebranded TPV Acebook Pro.  The Tylvx brand appears nowhere on the laptop itself or any of the packaging, but the TPV brand does on the underside of the unit (see picture).  In terms of hardware and price, this is a pretty solid laptop, but buying the Tylvx version may not be a good idea because of the software that's pre-installed.When you turn this laptop on, it asks you to create a local account and then boots directly into the home screen without trying to connect to the internet to verify the authenticity of the operating system or download updates.  Going into the computer settings shows the copy of Windows 11 as being activated and up to date, which sounds great...but it's absolutely not true.  This laptop arrived running Windows 11 23H2, which is so old it reached EOL last month on November 11th.  The current version of Windows 11 is 25H2, but the outdated version of Windows on the laptop was installed by Tylvx only last month, barely a week before it officially reached EOL.So why would Tylvx install version 23H2 of Windows 11 instead of 24H2 (which reaches EOL in 10 months) or 25H2, which is current?  Probably because Microsoft made changes after 23H2 to harden security and make it more difficult to modify parts of the OS.The version of Windows 11 installed by Tylvx is not standard and definitely has modified code because Windows completely bypasses online verification during setup only if code has been altered.  No version of Windows 11 from Microsoft does that.So this laptop is running a version of Windows that was custom-modified by Tylvx.  Since the hardware on this laptop is fully capable of officially running Windows 11, I can't think of any benevolent reason for Tylvx to do this.  Connecting the laptop to the internet with this version of Windows 11 installed is a potential security nightmare because, unless you happen to be a skilled software engineer, there's no way of knowing what other code Tylvx modified.The process of registering for the one-year warranty seems as sketchy as the OS, and there is no manual despite what it says on the QR Code sticker.Final Verdict:  Unless you plan to install your own OS, stay away from this Tylvx Professional Laptop or look for the same machine under the TPV AceBook Pro name instead.

I am putting out these key points so you can get a quick summary before reading any other reviews:1) The BIOS is American Megatrends2) The windows installation comes preinstalled; no included media with the laptop (Windows 11 Pro)3) The included mouse pad its absolutely garbage; I can hardly type this review without my mouse jumping around the screen4) The included charger is about as cheap as it gets; its a short 120VAC wall outlet plug that looks like something for a mobile phone. It plugs into a small DC port on the laptop (not a modern USB-C style charger)WITH THAT SAIDWe paid full price for this (around $400) which was a total rip. However, IT appears its available now for half that cost, which makes this a contender for actually useful... as long as you are paying mid $200's. With a USB mouse this could actually work a decent computer for a kid or something just to have laying around the house for small internet tasks.

Who is the new Razer Blade 16 best suited for? 
The Blade 16 is ideal for competitive gamers, streamers, and creators who want flagship RTX 5090 performance in a thin, premium 16-inch gaming laptop. 
Is the new Razer Blade 16 good for gaming? 
Yes. The Razer Blade 16 is built for high-performance gaming with up to NVIDIA GeForce RTX 5090 Laptop GPU and 165W TGP, delivering smooth frame rates in AAA titles and competitive esports games. 
What makes the new Razer Blade 16 different from other gaming laptops? 
It balances performance, display quality, portability, and premium build in one device rather than prioritizing only raw power or only portability. 
Should I choose Razer Blade 14, Blade 16, or Blade 18? 
The Blade 14 if you prioritize maximum portability. 
The Blade 16 if you want the best balance of performance, display immersion, and mobility. 
The Blade 18 if you want the largest display and closest-to-desktop experience. 
Is the Razer Blade 16 good for AI workloads? 
Yes. Powered by Intel Core Ultra 9 with up to 50 TOPS NPU performance and RTX 50 Series graphics, the Blade 16 supports AI-accelerated tasks such as content creation, rendering, and machine learning workflows.

items.text: Yes. The Razer Blade 16 is built for high-performance gaming with up to NVIDIA GeForce RTX 5090 Laptop GPU and 165W TGP, delivering smooth frame rates in AAA titles and competitive esports games.

items.name: What makes the new Razer Blade 16 different from other gaming laptops?
items.text: It balances performance, display quality, portability, and premium build in one device rather than prioritizing only raw power or only portability.

items.name: Should I choose Razer Blade 14, Blade 16, or Blade 18?
items.text: The Blade 14 if you prioritize maximum portability.  The Blade 16 if you want the best balance of performance, display immersion, and mobility.  The Blade 18 if you want the largest display and closest-to-desktop experience.

items.name: Is the Razer Blade 16 good for AI workloads?
items.text: Yes. Powered by Intel Core Ultra 9 with up to 50 TOPS NPU performance and RTX 50 Series graphics, the Blade 16 supports AI-accelerated tasks such as content creation, rendering, and machine learning workflows.

aPlusContent.title: From the manufacturer
aPlusContent.rawText:
From the manufacturer
Dell 15 Laptop 

A 15-inch laptop with a built-in camera HD, enlarged ergonomic keyboard and Intel core processors. 
Windows 11 brings you closer to what you love 

Family, friends, obsessions, music, creations—Windows 11 is the one place for it all. With a fresh feel and tools that make it easier to be efficient, it has what you need for whatever’s next. 
Effortlessly chic. Always efficient. 
Finish your to-do list in no time with the Dell 15, built for everyday computing with Intel core processors. 
Charge smarter 
Stay powered all day with energy-efficient battery management and ExpressCharge support, giving you an 80% charge in 1 hour. 
ExpressCharge must be enabled within Dell Power Manager software. System must be powered off or in hibernation mode for ExpressCharge feature to function. After charging has reached the stated capacity, charging speed will return to normal speed. Recommended for use with the provided Dell power adapter; not recommended with a smaller capacity power adapter. 
Stay connected to what you love 

Spend more screen time on the things you enjoy with Dell ComfortView software that helps reduce harmful blue light emissions to keep your eyes comfortable over extended viewing times. 
Ergonomic support 

Keep your wrists comfortable with lifted hinges that provide an ergonomic typing angle. 
Type with ease 

Write and calculate quickly with roomy keypads, separate numeric keypad and calculator hotkey. 
Adapt to any situation 

Adaptive thermals keep your PC running efficiently, whether at your desk or working from your lap. Your Dell 15 intelligently adjusts its power and thermals to keep it running smoothly. 
Environmentally conscious 

Your Dell 15 is designed with 30% post-consumer recycled plastic in the palmrest, and 50% post-consumer recycled plastic in the bottom cover, and ships in packaging made from 100% recycled and renewable materials. 
Percentage is of total plastic weight in product. Based on internal analysis, April 2025. 30% post-consumer recycled plastic in the palmrest and 50% post-consumer recycled plastic in the bottom cover. 
Ports and slots 
1. SD card reader | 2. USB 2.0 | 3. Universal audio jack | 4. Power jack | 5. HDMI 1.4 | 6. USB 3.2 Gen 1 Type-A | 7. USB 3.2 Gen 1 Type-C data only on plastic

This laptop with 8gb ram and a 512gb solid state hard drive fulfilled all my needs, with the exception of an Ethernet port. productPageReviews.reviewDescription: This refurbished laptop is in rough shape.  Scrapes and scratches throughout.  I do appreciate the upgrades made to the system (i5) and newer hard drive, so it is compatible with today's programs.  I'm finding the keys are very sticky - and not sure if thats due no use or if the under carriage is dirty.  I did open up the back of the computer and everything looks clean and in good shape.  The screen is a 14" matte, which works well for professional/business use.  This is not a gaming laptop.  I am happy with the speed to run programs.  I did have to download a few drivers and will have to purchase a WWAN card to use my mobile internet - but for a $180 laptop that used to run $1800 you can't really beat it.  I really appreciate the USB A ports as well as one USB C port.  So far, the battery life is holding up.  They do sell a dongle that connects from a USB C to this laptop (7.5mm) so you won't have to carry the big brick around.  But like I said, I think all in all, I've probably spent $250 bringing this dinosaur up to speed.

productPageReviews.reviewTitle: Unbeatable Workhorse for Dedicated Projects & Daily Tasks!Unbeatable Workhorse for Dedicated Projects & Daily Tasks!
productPageReviews.reviewDescription: I bought this laptop to be the low-power consuming, back-office system dedicated specifically to running a local SQL Server instance and a web interface for running data queries—and it has done just wonderful job doing so! This thing is an absolute beast for everyday performance!Setup was pretty straightforward—Windows allowed a simple setup without forcing a Microsoft account, which was a huge plus for getting right to work. Within minutes, I had SQL Server and SSMS installed alongside my dedicated deployment tools. Even with the backend tasks running, I haven’t experienced a single moment of lag or sluggishness... And the PC runs fairly cool.The combination of the Intel Quad-Core N95 processor and 16GB of RAM is the 'secret sauce' here—delivering fluid, reliable performance while keeping power consumption relatively low.Screen: The 1080P IPS display looks great with crisp, sharp visuals during video testing on YouTube, and the hinge opens flat up to a full 180-degree angle for easy (physical) screen sharing.The built-in camera works smoothly for "Teams," and the onboard speakers do a functional job for everyday audio and meetings.Premium Metal Shell: It feels sleek, sturdy, and well-built—definitely higher quality than expected for the price.Battery life has been excellent for long work sessions, and modern touches like WiFi 6 and Type-C charging make it fast to connect and easy to keep powered up.Bottom line, if you need a reliable, low-power, and well-built machine for specialized workloads, coding, or office productivity, this is a fantastic choice. Highly recommended!

productPageReviews.reviewTitle: A no-frills laptop that looks premiumA no-frills laptop that looks premium
productPageReviews.reviewDescription: This is an easy-to-use laptop that does everything you’d expect it to. The implementation of Windows 11 is great (not using an old OS like Windows 10) and the laptop works seamlessly with my webcam, docking station, internet connection, external USB drives, printer, etc. (It worked with my Brother printer without my having to install any software.)The keyboard layout is fairly standard, with a few exceptions you can quickly get used to. The keys are responsive and easy to type with. They have decent travel and are nice and clicky - but still quiet. No mushy mealy keys here!Since the laptop isn’t by a big-name manufacturer, it doesn’t have a lot of additional programs provided by that manufacturer. However, that can be an advantage, because it’s not junked up with apps you’ll never use, and you’re not constantly pestered to set up an account with the manufacturer so they can put you on their email list.The laptop has three USB-A ports and only one available USB-C (assuming you’re using the other USB-C for the included power cable). I would rather have more USB-C ports, given today’s needs. Also, the USB-A ports seem a little sticky; it takes a bit of pushing and pulling to get plugs in and out. There’s an HDMI port and a slot for a memory card.PS, the logo looks pretty cool actually. It's both professional and gamer all at once!When the battery is fully charged, the indicator says it will last for four hours. There is no sign of software that will prevent the battery from charging beyond 80 percent or so, which some manufacturers provide to prolong battery life, but being able to charge via USB-C is a massive quality of life improvement since you are NEVER without a charger. Total gamechanger.Laptops are getting pretty generic these days, and this one is good example: no splashy manufacturer’s name or apps, just meat and potatoes. The manufacturer advertises support via WhatsApp, accessed through a QR code on a sticker on the keyboard. I haven't contacted them yet, but it feels much nicer than having just an e-mail address or some awful IVR phone tree when I need help

productPageReviews.reviewTitle: Lightweight and easy to take anywhere
productPageReviews.reviewDescription: My main purpose in buying this laptop is for a lightweight everyday laptop that I can take anywhere. This is exactly what I was looking for, it’s super light, turns on quickly, doesn’t have a ton of programs opening up when you turn it on, and it’s battery life lasts more than long enough for my needs. I tend to take it out without even bringing my charger and it works for most of the day without issues for light use. I think it’s a very good value especially since comparable computers from the big brands were an extra $200 more expensive. Definitely a good buy if you’re looking for something small that you can use daily for basic tasks.

productPageReviews.reviewTitle: Great computer, especially for the price I paid.
productPageReviews.reviewDescription: I had already ordered a T495 with a Ryzen 3700u from Lenovo with similar specs for $950 (a substantial discount from their list price) when I saw this item on Amazon for $650. I ordered from Amazon and will send the other one back to Lenovo as soon as it gets here.The benchmarks for the 3500u actually seem to beat out the more expensive 3700u which I had already ordered. I don't know what explains this, but according to my research this computer should perform about the same as the one with the better processor.I was a little concerned about the screen because none of the reviews I found online where for a T495 with touch. In fact the screen is just fine, if slightly too dim. I haven't had a situation where the brightness isn't enough, but it would be nice to have a little headroom in this regard.Everything about the computer is really nice. Very solid build, looks and feels great. The keyboard feels good and the touchpad is decent, though not as good as my old Surface Book 2. The hinges are sturdy and hold the display at whatever angle I need. The ports are all great and feel solid; nothing is loose in them.Unfortunately the provided 65W charger doesn't provide for fast-charging, so I'll be upgrading that. I have a 16 GB RAM stick coming which by all accounts will give the computer a substantial boost in performance thanks to opening up dual-channel RAM usage. With a $60 16gb RAM stick and about the same amount for a bigger SSD I have a great computer at a bargain price. I doubt I could do much better without getting something used.

productPageReviews.reviewDescription: I didn’t expect to be this impressed. The Lenovo IdeaPad hits that rare sweet spot between affordability and genuinely solid performance. Battery life has been consistent as well, easily carrying me through a full workday with mixed use.What surprised me most is how quiet it runs. Setup was fast, Wi-Fi is strong, and everything just works without fuss — which is more than I can say for several laptops I’ve owned in the same price range.If you need a dependable everyday laptop that doesn’t feel like a compromise, this one overdelivers. productPageReviews.reviewTitle: ASUS ROG Strix Scar 18 — Started Amazing, Fell Apart in Hours
productPageReviews.reviewDescription: I bought the Scar 18 expecting a monster. And at first, that’s exactly what it looked like. The first couple hours were perfect — smooth performance, great FPS, VR running better than I’d ever seen, and flat‑screen games looking incredible. I genuinely thought I finally found the laptop that could handle everything I threw at it.Then, in a matter of hours, it all fell apart.It started with small glitches…A few screen tears here and there.A weird flicker.A gray flash that didn’t make sense.I brushed it off at first — new drivers, new hardware, maybe just early quirks.But it didn’t stop.It got worse.Then came the crashesGames started freezing.VR apps would lock up.Windows itself would hang or stutter.Everything that was smooth earlier suddenly felt unstable.I wasn’t tuning anymore — I was babysitting the system.The anti‑aliasing ghosting wasn’t normal ghosting — it was THREE DESKTOPSThis was the moment I realized something was seriously wrong.Moving the mouse or a window left a triple ghost image behind it — three faint copies of the desktop trailing across the screen. Not in a game. Not in VR.In Windows itself.It looked like the entire display pipeline was desyncing.And once that started, it never stopped.VR went from “almost perfect” to “unusable”Every fix made it worse.Every tweak broke something else.Performance dropped, stability tanked, and the whole VR experience collapsed.I wasn’t improving anything — I was fighting the laptop nonstop.Then the problems spread to flat‑screen gamesTomb Raider — a game that should run flawlessly on hardware this strong — suddenly had:ghostingtearingunstable frametimesrandom crashesweird motion artifactsIt felt like the system was falling apart piece by piece.The worst part? It happened FASTThis wasn’t a slow decline over weeks.It wasn’t a bad update months later.It happened within hours of owning it.One moment it was perfect.The next, it was a mess of tears, gray screens, crashes, ghosting, and instability that spread from VR into Windows and then into every game I tried.Final VerdictThe Scar 18 has insane specs, but the experience I had was exhausting. I expected a powerhouse. What I got was a system I had to babysit, troubleshoot, and fight constantly — only to end up getting nowhere.For the price, I expected stability.Instead, I got a laptop that fell apart faster than I could fix it.
productPageReviews.reviewedIn: Reviewed in the United States on June 29, 2026

productPageReviews.reviewDescription: This is a powerful laptop, no doubt.  I loved the way it made my games look for the first week or so.  But now I am in a rabbit hole, that I can't find my way out of, and the laptop that I spend SO MUCH money on, is useless to perform the only task I purchased it for.I am unable to game with this laptop, because it randomly crashes and black screens in the middle of online gaming.  Gaming is built around progression and statistics.  Losing all my long earned inventory, or causing my team to lose because I cannot see, or I crashed,  or ruining my stats multiple times a night is the anthesis of a gaming laptop.  Its an anti-gaming laptop.Before you purchase this laptop, or any Asus laptop, please do a simple google search "Asus laptop black screen"I have done so much, I have done driver installs, driver cleaning utilities, bios updates, armory crate (asus software) uninstall tool, clean reinstall, and on and on.  I have followed step by step guides, Asus forum solutions, AI solutions.  Sometimes I can game for an hour and a half straight, sometimes I boot up my computer, and start a game I crash in three minutes.  -this is not a thermal issue, I may play for 22 minutes and black screen reboot, and then I may play for 5 minutes black screen, reboot, then I may play for an hour and a half, black screen, reboot.  Same game, same resolutions, same settings, same night.  When I was considering a gaming laptop for my son, we went with an HP omen, he has had no problems.  He games more often than I do, and his PC seems more reliable.Don't know what to say, not trying to be hyper critical, but I am regretting my purchase.I am changing my reveiw.  It turns out windows 11 is the culprit.  A recent update fixed a couple week clash with nVidia software, and the laptop is functioning well.running some very hi resolutions for long periods of time.

productPageReviews.reviewTitle: Biggest RTX 5090 scam I've seen in years - pure lottery whether it even works
productPageReviews.reviewDescription: I've been an ASUS fanboy for 7–8 years straight - ROG laptops, motherboards, GPUs, everything. Never once let me down in gaming or heavy programming workloads. That's why when the 2025 ROG Strix SCAR 18 with RTX 5090 dropped I didn't even hesitate - bought it the second it was available.Four days later I was already losing my mind.Black / gray screen crash in literally every demanding game after 5–40 seconds. I tried everything known to man:• Clean Windows 10 + Windows 11 (every build including latest insider)• Every NVIDIA driver branch from 551.xx to 572.xx (full DDU wipe in safe mode every single time)• BIOS rollback + latest BIOS flash• Every Armoury Crate power profile (Silent → Performance → Turbo → Manual)• iGPU disabled, hybrid mode off, pure dGPU only• Undervolts, overclocks, stock - nothing matteredThe ONLY thing that stopped the crashes was installing G-Helper and forcibly capping Core Clock at 1600–1650 MHz in Ultimate mode.After that - no more black screens… but the 5090 was running at roughly 40–55% of its real potential.For 3500–4500+ dollars I basically got a prettied-up 4080/4090-class laptop from two years ago.Turns out this is a massive widespread issue specifically with ASUS RTX 5090 implementations (especially the 175W–200W variants in SCAR 18 and SCAR 16).Huge threads on Reddit, ASUS ROG forums, Discord - tons of people in late 2025–early 2026 reporting exactly the same nightmare.In the end I gave up and returned it.My hardware-nerd friends (guys who daily bench and reverse-engineer this stuff) unanimously told me:"Right now just grab ASUS with 5080 or 5070 Ti - same real-world gaming performance, zero of these insane driver/BIOS lottery problems so far."The laptop itself is gorgeous - screen is insane, keyboard feels premium, speakers are surprisingly good, cooling looks monstrous on paper.But when you're paying flagship money for a silicon & firmware lottery where your 5090 might decide to work at half power or not work at all - that's straight-up unacceptable.Buy this thing only if you're ready to:Spend 2–4 weeks dancing with BIOS, drivers and third-party toolsBe mentally prepared for RMA/returnPray that by the time you read this ASUS finally released a proper fix (as of January 6, 2026 - they still haven't)Very sad to write this about ASUS.Hope this review saves at least a couple of people from throwing 4k+ into the trash and months of frustration.

productPageReviews.reviewDescription: Who it’s for:Students, light creators, and anyone who wants a capable everyday laptop that doesn’t fall apart the moment you unplug it. (Note, Laptops run better when connected to wall power and drop in performance when on battery power to extend battery life.)Who should look elsewhere:Users who prioritize silent operation, premium build, or sustained heavy workloads/modern gaming. This wouldn't be a good work laptop either since it lacks certain ports (Ethernet, full USB4/Thunderbolt) and security features such as a fingerprint reader, advanced BIOS security options, and an IR camera for facial recognition.The Lenovo IdeaPad Slim 3 with the Ryzen 7 8840HS, 16Gb of DDR5-5600, 512gb SSD, 60Wh battery is a lightweight, budget-friendly laptop that performs above its price range in several important areas, though it comes with some clear downsides.Design & Build:At first glance the Slim 3 feels like a typical thin-and-light plastic laptop. The chassis is reasonably solid for the price, but it’s not without flaws. There’s noticeable flex in the keyboard deck when twisting, pressing down on the center keyboard area will make it flex inward, and the screen is particularly thin and flexible — I wouldn’t recommend picking the laptop up by the display. The trackpad has a good click feel and reliable tap detection, but it’s offset to the left, which means your right palm often rests on it when using the spacebar if you choose to do some light gaming on it. The barrel charger is functional but less convenient than modern USB-C charging.Performance:This is where the Slim 3 surprised me. The Ryzen 7 8840HS (Zen 4) delivers strong multi-core and excellent single-thread performance. In Cinebench and real-world use it consistently outperformed my higher-clocked but older Ryzen 9 6900HX laptop, especially when running on battery.Everyday responsiveness is good — browser tabs, multitasking, and general snappiness feel quick.Gaming:The results were more mixed but still respectable for a non gaming laptop. Stardew Valley ran without issues and was very comfortable to play maxing out at the games preset max 60 FPS, Assassin’s Creed Black Flag ran at 45–60 FPS on High settings, and Cyberpunk 2077 stayed somewhat playable at 25-45 FPS on Low/Medium even on battery power (something my other laptop failed at spectacularly). This laptop is not meant for modern AAA gaming but will handle indie titles and older games just well if you want to do some gaming on the go. If you play games on this laptop I highly recommend having the charger on hand.Thermals & Noise:This is the biggest weakness. Under sustained load the single fan gets loud and the chassis becomes warm to hot. It never became dangerously hot in my testing, but the noise and heat are definitely noticeable during longer sessions or games. On lighter tasks it settles down reasonably well. I suggest pairing it with a laptop cooling pad if you don't mind using one.Battery & Display:The 60Wh battery performed better than expected under mixed use. Under extreme workload/gaming you're going to get about 2hr so keep a charger on hand. When doing light browsing or scrolling though social media/watching videos and movies you'll get closer to 6-8hrs depending on brightness and if the laptop can breath well. Choking the fan intake will cause it to heat up and lose performance and battery power through excess heat so keep it on a hard clean and surface. The touchscreen is a nice bonus for the price, though the panel itself is average IPS 1920x1200 with up to 300 nita of brightness and average color accuracy. The reds will look orange and the greens will appear slightly yellow. Might be an issue for anyone doing video or photo editing.Final Thoughts:The IdeaPad Slim 3 with the 8840HS is a strong contender if you want a portable, responsive laptop that can still handle light-to-moderate gaming and creative work, especially on battery. It’s not the quietest or coolest machine, and the build quality has some soft spots, but the combination of performance, efficiency, touchscreen, and price makes it hard to ignore.

productPageReviews.reviewTitle: Solid Performance For Everyday UseSolid Performance For Everyday Use
productPageReviews.reviewDescription: I bought this laptop mainly for everyday tasks like browsing and streaming but wanted something that could also handle light gaming on the side. The Ryzen 7 processor handles multitasking well, I can have several tabs open along with other programs running without any slowdown. Games that are not too demanding run smoothly and the Radeon graphics handle them better than I expected for this price range.The screen looks sharp and colors come out clear, which makes a difference whether I am watching videos or playing something visually heavy. The 1TB storage gives me plenty of room for games, files, and downloads without worrying about running out of space anytime soon. Startup and load times are fast thanks to the SSD, nothing feels sluggish even when switching between apps quickly.Battery life holds up fine for daily use around the house and the keyboard feels comfortable for long typing sessions. Wifi 6 keeps the connection stable even when streaming or downloading larger files. This has been a solid laptop for someone who wants one machine that handles both work and casual gaming without needing to buy two separate devices.

productPageReviews.reviewTitle: Good for browsing, but no dedicated graphics
productPageReviews.reviewDescription: I think this is a good laptop for its price, but I can't recommend it without some kind of dedicated graphics. While this laptop can definitely browse the web and play movies, it will have big problems with any application that tries to display complicated graphics, like CAD programs. If you are in computer science or engineering for your college major, you need to look at a different buy, but otherwise this is okay. For me, I feel like 15.6" is a bit large, but that size allows for a number keypad, which is on this laptop. Just be careful, since the power button is in the corner of the keypad (above the ./Del key) and pressing that will turn off your PC unless you change it.Our of the box, this PC came with its charger and on a full charge it claimed to be able to last 10 hours. However, despite "10H" being shown in the battery estimate, this dropped to 90% after around 20 minutes, possibly because I was installing some software. I think that the actual battery life when using this laptop for medium-intensity tasks will turn out to be around 5 hours, half of what the absolute maximum is.The trackpad is pretty large, which is good, but I feel like the keyboard could have better ergonomics for typing. Additionally, I wish that the lid didn't pull up the bottom of the laptop when opening it. My other windows laptop doesn't do that, so it's a bit annoying that it happens with this one.This is still a good buy if you just need a computer to use, and it comes with a Windows software license on it, and it directly lets you set up a local account without needing to sign into Microsoft, but if you'll need anything that might involve graphics or AI, you'll want a laptop with a dedicated internal GPU and/or NPU.

productPageReviews.reviewTitle: Great budget laptop and feels really nice
productPageReviews.reviewDescription: Great budget laptop and it has USB C charging which is great because you don't have to have a certain charger for it. This laptop feels nice and has an AWESOME picture thanks to it's IPS display. This is a good computer for work or just browsing the internet, gaming on it though is lack luster no dedicated GPU in this laptop. The graphics are handled by the CPU so it's alright but for gaming you want a dedicated GPU.I love the fact that both the top plate and bottom plate on this laptop are an alloy metal and gives it some weight, I actually like the additional weight on a laptop it gives it a bit more presence in my mind.I did open it up to see about upgrades that you can do, I know that was a question when I bought it for me. It has a single DDR stick of RAM in it and that's it, I mean you could upgrade that to a single stick of 32GB RAM but still going to be in single channel mode. It has the typical slot for the NVME drive and no expansion slot so you can't put another NVME drive in there for storage.  Both the NVME and RAM sticks were off brand, but perform well.Oh the best part of this system is it's a bloat free version of Windows 11 installed, no third party apps and stuff like that to slow your system down, just your basic Windows 11 installed. I ran a program to make sure there was no malicious software installed and didn't find anything.Overall for the price it's a great budget laptop that feels good while using it. It's responsive enough to get work done and to get on the internet and watch YouTube and stuff like that.

productPageReviews.reviewTitle: Unexpected Ryzen 7 Upgrade Makes This Laptop a Steal!
productPageReviews.reviewDescription: I ordered this KAIGERR laptop because the specs looked great for the price, especially the 16GB RAM, 512GB SSD, and the advertised Intel N97 processor. But when I received it, I found out it actually came with a Ryzen 7 5825U! That's a significantly more powerful processor, so I was pleasantly surprised. The laptop feels well-built, yet thin and light; and the 15.6-inch FHD screen is crisp and clear. Performance-wise, it's been fantastic for everyday tasks like browsing, word processing, streaming, and even some light photo editing. It handles multitasking without any slowdown, which is great. I haven't had any issues with the touchpad or anything else, so far.Now, it's a lesser-known brand, so I was initially a bit cautious. Some of the other reviews mentioned concerns about bloatware or spyware, but I haven't found anything suspicious on my machine. I ran some scans, and everything came back clean. I also checked the network activity, and nothing seemed out of the ordinary. Still, it's something to keep in mind if you're particularly security-conscious. It might be worth doing a clean install of Windows if you have any doubts. However, for me, everything has been running smoothly. The battery life has also been pretty decent, lasting me most of the day on a single charge.Overall, I'm extremely happy with this laptop, especially with the surprise Ryzen 7 upgrade. It's a fantastic value for the money, offering excellent performance and a great set of features. If you're looking for a powerful and affordable laptop, this one is definitely worth considering. The unexpected processor upgrade I received makes it an even better deal than advertised!

productPageReviews.reviewTitle: Great hardware! A lot to love about the machine.  Complete fail on support.
productPageReviews.reviewDescription: The laptop is surprisingly good!  It's not the greatest power house and not for high end gaming but I've tried some online and some MMORP games that were smooth as silk.  I didn't have settings at their highest but the screen is big and beautiful so it's really a fine system.This is the first machine I've owned that didn't have a power supply other than a usb C.  That's interesting and probably something that is coming on strong.  Not having a brick power supply is pretty nice.The touchpad is large and includes a fingerprint sensor in the top left.  It works just fine and is actually functional and convenient.The keyboard is backlit and I like it but it goes dark very quickly if you aren't typing.  Number pad is pretty standard and the keys themselves are pleasant enough.Wifi and bluetooth work as they should and connections were easy with no problems at all.  Wifi and bluetooth stay connected and stable which is always a plus.With a total of 5 usb connections (one of the C ports is used for power) it's really great for accessories and it makes the portability factor awesome.  If you travel and hate running out of ports and needing a hub then this laptop is a hero.The machine is super quiet and never seems to get very hot.  It's a pleasure to use without needing a cooling pad.Expandabilty is amazing on this machine.  Serously huge potential for RAM and SSD expansion.  I maxed out on both and it's amazingly fast in general.  Nothing work related even slows it down.I love this machine, it's extremely functional without breaking the bank.  I bought one for my son in college and he loves it as well.  I'd recommend this machine to anyone that isn't in CAD related endeavors.Nothing in life is perfect and while the hardware here is great, the support is terrible.  If you're not someone that needs support or a helpline then this one is great, if you do need support it doesn't get much worse.The biggest problem with the laptop is the completely sad documentation and support system.  Don't expect anything from the the support system because it's 100% useless and apparently not based in English so they don't answer their tech requests in anything but the most general and not helpful ways.  They sent me links to videos that had literally nothing to do with my questions.  BAD.  BAD. BAD.  They really suck for support.

productPageReviews.reviewTitle: Computer great, refurbish quality missed a major issue.Computer great, refurbish quality missed a major issue.
productPageReviews.reviewDescription: This review is mostly about the refurbish service, the computer itself is absolutely fantastic.  My expectations for a refurbished computer was that I would get something that would show very modest wear, but work perfectly. I was delighted when I first opened my new Lenovo computer. The screen, keyboard, and touchpad appeared like it was brand new had never been touched. I was initially delighted with my purchase and started loading software and restoring my data. On the second day however, I noticed some unusual indentations around the power button. As I explored it further, I found that the computer had probably been dropped on its side. It actually bent the case enough to make the SD card slot unusable. It also makes the USB connectors quite tight (which may not actually be a bad thing in and of itself - but it's not right). The bottom of the case shows a physical crack and I am moderately concerned about whether there's some hairline fractures or other damage that isn't immediately obvious. The bottom line is, I've decided to keep the computer since it seems to be working fine and I really appreciate the pristine screen and keyboard that I received. I don't use the SD card slot so it's not a big deal to me for that. But I guess I'm just a little disappointed to have received a laptop that was clearly dropped hard enough to bend the case.  I know this happed before shipping as the box it was delivered in showed no signs of any drop.  It is a bit of a testament to the high-quality build that Lenovo puts into their computers but not a great example of careful oversight on the Amazon reconditioning service.  I think they should have been more descriptive about this kind of damage on this particular item (maybe offered it with a bit more discount?)

productPageReviews.reviewTitle: If you need a push here it is!
productPageReviews.reviewDescription: Bought this laptop the lenova thinkpad E16 G2 back in sometime last year on sale and I haven't regretted it a single bit. My wife and I both find it to be snappy between tasks and never lags while doing general day to day tasks such as emails, surfing the web,  backing up our drives, Microsoft office suite, etc. We don't game so I cannot tell you if this would suit your needs if looking for that type of lato however it is only a 952mb processor which if I'm not mistaken gaming requires 4 gigs or better. The storage on this device is great and is a solid 1tb. Windows 11 has operated flawlessly without any tickets to lenova concerning our device.Now that being said. I have the ryzen 7 version and while I thought it would be able to handle using design software such as canva and adobe I would have to advise you look for a better processor. This one WILL do what you need however, I doubt CAD etc would be able to function with any sort of quickness. I've learned a lot about how rendering and speeds are more than just ram now which this laptop has plenty of! In fact this is the most ram I've ever had on a latop or PC so for what we do it is perfect.Speakers generate nice loud crisp not distorted sound quality and video on it looks above average. Lenova support has been excellent though I initially had an issue that I was the cause of which we fixed without any issue. I would recommend this laptop for sure!

description: The MSI Crosshair A16 HX 16-inch gaming laptop delivers QHD+ clarity and high-refresh responsiveness for competitive gaming, streaming, and creative workflows. It runs Windows 11 Home and is powered by an AMD Ryzen 9 8940HX processor, enabling strong multi-core performance for demanding titles, video editing, and productivity suites. The 16-inch 2560 x 1600 IPS display with 16:10 aspect ratio and 240 Hz refresh rate offers sharp detail, extra vertical workspace, and fluid motion that enhances fast-paced shooters and timeline scrubbing. GeForce RTX 5060 Laptop graphics bring advanced ray tracing and AI-enhanced rendering to supported games and creative apps, providing smooth visuals and efficient performance. Wireless connectivity with Wi Fi 6E keeps online matches responsive, while Bluetooth 5.3 supports modern headsets, controllers, and other peripherals for a clean, cable-light setup. A 720p HD webcam handles everyday video calls and casual streaming; with proper lighting and angle adjustments, it produces clear images for meetings, classes, or team chats. The audio system is tuned for clarity so in-game communication and conference voices remain intelligible. A 4-cell Lithium Ion battery is designed to balance mobility with the power of the HX-class processor and RTX graphics, supporting extended study sessions, office work, or entertainment away from the outlet. The chassis weighs about 5.51 lbs, offering a sturdy yet portable form factor for moving between home, campus, or events. Connectivity includes a USB 3.2 Gen 2 Type C port, three USB 3.2 Gen 1 Type A ports, and HDMI 2.1, giving you flexibility for external monitors, input devices, and accessories. With its fast display, powerful CPU and GPU combination, modern wireless features, integrated HD camera, and dependable battery, the Crosshair A16 HX is aimed at gamers and creators who want a single system for immersive play and serious work.
features: 【Instant Gratification】Crosshair A16 HX drops you instantly into smooth, high-frame-rate gaming with its 16-inch QHD+ 240 Hz IPS display, responsive keyboard, and quick-wake design. The portable 5.51 lbs chassis moves effortlessly from desk to LAN parties, while the AMD Ryzen 9 processor and RTX 5060 GPU ensure solid performance for competitive play, streaming, or casual sessions right out of the box.

【Processor & Operating System】AMD Ryzen 9 8940HX (2.4–5.3 GHz) powers intense multitasking, game rendering, and content creation, paired with Windows 11 Home for modern security, intuitive navigation, Game Pass integration, and seamless app support. This combo keeps you productive in school, work, or esports without interruptions or slowdowns during peak usage.

【Display】16-inch 2560x1600 QHD+ IPS panel with 16:10 ratio and 240 Hz refresh delivers extra vertical space for maps, timelines, and docs, plus ultra-fluid motion for tracking enemies or editing video. High brightness and color accuracy make it ideal for bright rooms, HDR content, and precise creative work.

【Graphics】GeForce RTX 5060 Laptop GPU with 8 GB GDDR7 handles ray tracing, DLSS upscaling, and high-res textures at QHD+, boosting frame rates in shooters, RPGs, and apps. It accelerates rendering, streaming, and AI effects, giving creators and gamers reliable power for demanding sessions.

【Tech Specs】4-cell Li-ion battery supports mobile gaming and work; 720p HD webcam for calls; Wi-Fi 6E, Bluetooth 5.3; ports: USB-C PD, 3x USB-A, HDMI 2.1. At 5.51 lbs with solid build, it balances power and portability for school, office, or events.
